updates.name: Debra Hernandez
updates.bio: Executive Director of SECOORA, the nonprofit U.S. IOOS regional association serving North Carolina, South Carolina, Georgia and Florida. A Clemson-trained civil engineer with expertise in ocean and coastal engineering, management, and policy, she has sat on the Ocean Studies Board of the National Academies and a federal ocean research advisory panel, and has chaired the IOOS Association.
updates.research_interests: coastal and ocean engineering; coastal and ocean management and policy; regional coastal ocean observing (U.S. IOOS)
updates.current_affiliation: Southeast Coastal Ocean Observing Regional Association (SECOORA)
updates.notes: Contact page (200) lists 'Debra Hernandez Executive Director'; also listed as Executive Director at https://ioos.noaa.gov/regions/secoora/. Bio source is a 2021 seminar page. ORCID registry search found only 0009-0007-3079-1033 (Debra Hernandez, no employment/affiliation) - not adopted. No personal profile page found; homepage_url is the SECOORA contact/staff page.

updates.name: Dennis L. Todey
updates.bio: Director of the USDA Midwest Climate Hub in Ames, Iowa. Trained in meteorology and agricultural meteorology at Iowa State (BS, PhD). He was previously South Dakota's State Climatologist and an associate professor at South Dakota State University, and he has led the American Association of State Climatologists as its president.

updates.name: Dennis R. Helsel
updates.bio: Owner and lead scientist of Practical Stats, a firm providing statistics training and consulting for environmental and water-resources work. Holds a PhD in environmental science and engineering from Virginia Tech; lead author of the USGS text Statistical Methods in Water Resources and of a Wiley book on censored environmental data. Recipient of the Interior Department's Distinguished Service Award (2007).
updates.research_interests: applied statistics for water resources; statistical analysis of censored environmental data (nondetects)
updates.notes: Identity tied to USGS via the USGS textbook Statistical Methods in Water Resources (Helsel & Hirsch) on https://practicalstats.com/. No fetched page states USGS retirement/emeritus status, so status reflects current consulting role. ORCID 0000-0001-9324-1708 (Dennis Helsel; PhD Virginia Tech, matching credentials page) exists but lists no employment, so per the strict rule it was NOT adopted - candidate for manual verification.
updates.evidence: He is the owner and lead scientist of Practicalstats, a statistics training and consulting firm.

updates.name: Derek Aday
updates.bio: Professor and Dean & Director of the Batten School & Virginia Institute of Marine Science. Trained at Louisiana State (MS) and Illinois (PhD), his research addressed fish conservation and management, invasive species, fish population and community ecology, and contaminant effects on fish; he is an AFS Fellow and editor-in-chief of Transactions of the American Fisheries Society.
updates.research_interests: aquatic ecology; conservation biology; fishery science; environmental toxicology; invasive species dynamics; population and community ecology of freshwater and marine fishes; mercury and endocrine-disrupting contaminants in fish
updates.current_affiliation: Batten School & Virginia Institute of Marine Science (VIMS)

updates.name: Devendra M. Amatya
updates.bio: Research hydrologist at the USDA Forest Service Southern Research Station, with a PhD in soil and water from North Carolina State University. His studies cover coastal-plain forested-wetland hydrology, including Santee Experimental Forest watersheds, forest evapotranspiration, hydroclimatic extremes on experimental-forest reference watersheds, and design flows for forest road culverts.
updates.research_interests: hydrology of coastal plain forested wetlands and poorly drained pine forests; Santee Experimental Forest paired-watershed and longleaf pine restoration studies; forest evapotranspiration; hydroclimatic extremes on reference watersheds; water table depth modeling; design flood estimation for forest road culverts (CULVERT tool)
updates.current_affiliation: USDA Forest Service, Southern Research Station
updates.notes: Profile moved to research.fs.usda.gov/about/people/devendra.m.amatya (200; server needs HTTP/1.1, flaky). Page displays ORCID 0000-0003-2641-9267, matching existing value - unchanged. updates.name: Douglas A. Burns
updates.bio: Research hydrologist at the USGS New York Water Science Center since 1987, now coordinating the USGS Next Generation Water Observing System effort in the Delaware River Basin. With degrees from Virginia (MS) and SUNY-ESF (PhD), he studies watershed biogeochemistry: acid rain, nitrogen and mercury cycling, and climate-driven high flows. He has also directed the National Acid Precipitation Assessment Program.
updates.research_interests: watershed biogeochemistry and hydrology; effects of acidic deposition on ecosystems; nitrogen cycling in watersheds; environmental mercury cycling; effects of suburban land use, forest harvesting and climate change on streams; climate-change effects on high streamflows; surface water quality
